before: You came for me. Twice, if you count the woods. I'm counting the woods.
after: You came back for me. Down there, on purpose. I'm going to need a while to stop being cross about it.

before: You have been my prisoner for five minutes, and you have given me no trouble. Let me give you something in return.
after: You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Today you start. Let me give you something to start with.

before: Druid Sorrel clasps her hands. "You brought Billie's herd home? The goat, the pig and that raccoon? Then the stream owes you a bridge."
after: Moss Mulligan hops up from the bank. "You got Billie's herd home? The goat, the pig AND the raccoon? Then the stream owes you a bridge."

before: Druid Sorrel shakes her head gently. "I only grow bridges for people who have helped the herd, and Billie Muckfoot's animals have got out again.
after: Moss Mulligan tucks her hands behind her back. "Sorry! I only grow bridges for people who have helped the herd, and Billie Muckfoot's animals have got out again.

before: Round them up for Billie, then come back to me, and I will grow you a way across."
after: Round them up for Billie, then come back to me, and I will grow you a way across. No thorns. Promise."

before: Druid Sorrel grows this one for anyone who helps Billie Muckfoot round up the herd.
after: Moss Mulligan grows this one for anyone who helps Billie Muckfoot round up the herd.

before: The herd's home and it's plotting. Thanks! Druid Sorrel at the centre bridge will grow you a crossing now. Tell her I sent you.
after: The herd's home and it's plotting. Thanks! Moss Mulligan at the centre bridge will grow you a crossing now. Tell her I sent you.

before: Shirt number two hundred and thirteen. Very proud of it. Notice my form?
after: Shirt number two hundred and twelve. Very proud of it. Notice my form?

before: The last guard before the Chamber of the Model: a warden whose job is to keep everyone away from the table. (Elite)
after: The last guard before the Model Room: a warden whose job is to keep everyone away from the table. (Elite)

before: The Scale Model Chamber
after: The Model Room

before: The Chamber of the Model is round and domed, and in its centre stands a table the size of a house: a perfect miniature of {kingdom}.
after: The Model Room is round and domed, and in its centre stands a table the size of a house: a perfect miniature of {kingdom}.

before: At half health a reserve guard steps off a pedestal: a 1/1 Militia joins.
after: At half health a reserve guard steps off a pedestal: a 1/1 Reserve Guard joins.

before: Gerald
after: Nugget

before: The Colonel
after: Big Lou

before: PELL FAMILY PARLOR
after: PELL FAMILY PARLOUR

before: The deceased are asked to remain in their parlors until a permit has been approved. Please do not wander.
after: The deceased are asked to remain in their parlours until a permit has been approved. Please do not wander.

before: Widow Pell's husband has sat in the family parlor for three years because his burial permit loops forever. It needs the Stamp of Final Approval, somewhere in Grave Row.
after: Widow Pell's husband has sat in the family parlour for three years because his burial permit loops forever. It needs the Stamp of Final Approval, somewhere in Grave Row.

before: Attention, citizens. (a cough) This is a loudspeaker. Nobody is on the other end.
after: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved. It is just weather. It seems to be managing.

before: The Alchemist's tri-Path crafting is unlocked (no tri-Path recipes exist yet).
after: The Alchemist's cauldron now takes three Paths at once: brew their essence into a tri-Path card.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: ...Cold. Leaves in my mouth. Great start.
after: Ugh... Where am I? Who am I?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I reach for my name. Nothing. Not even the shape of one.
after: I search for my name. For how I got here. But I find nothing.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Two hands, one of them shaking. I'll start with the other one. ...And I'm not alone.
after: I try to rise, but I am weak. A low groan escapes my mouth.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Easy. Stay down. Hands like ice, pulse like a rabbit's. We'll fix that later.
after: Easy. Stay down. Gather what strength you have. I can't imagine its much after what they put you through.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: A friend. That's all I can give you, and it's already more than is safe.
after: A friend. That's all I can say, there isn't much time.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand like you used to... never mind, just your hand.
after: Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Faint will do - it has to. Those torches on the ridge are looking for us.
after: That will have to do. The path-ologists are hunting us.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Tell me: which Path resonates the strongest within you?
after: Tell me: which Path resonates within you?

speaker: The Rescuer
before: That one, then. Hold on to it, and it will hold on to you.
after: That one, then. Cling to it. Hopefully you can walk the others again soon.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Hear that? They're close. I'll draw them off the other way. They know my face; let them chase it.
after: Hear that? They're close, but they do not know of this place, few do.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: So you go on alone. Don't thank me. Thank me when you're somewhere with a roof. Go!
after: You must escape. I'll draw them off the other way. I'll find you if I make it out.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: ...Gone, toward the torches. I never even asked their name.
after: She's gone, and shes leading them away. By the way their shouting I do not want to be caught by them.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: The trees close up that way. The cave, then.
after: The trees are too dense to pass through. To the cave.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Torches that way, cave this way. I'll take the one that isn't looking for me.
after: Whoever that was said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever is inside the cave seems like a better option than those path-ologists.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: ...Hm. Woken. For this. Another of the little scavengers, I suppose.
after: ...Hm. Woken from my slumber.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: ...No. Not that. You smell familiar. Like old stone, and cold nights, in a house I used to keep.
after: It has been some time since anyone has walked this path.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: The house does not open for just anyone. ...Show me.
after: No matter. Only one may pass, and he is long dead.

speaker: (name card)
before: Keeper of the House
after: Hollow Warden

speaker: Hollow Warden
before: ...You smell familiar. Show me your hands.
after: I shall perform my duty.

speaker: (battle UI)
before: At half health the Warden wakes a little more: a 1/1 Cave Echo rises beside it.
after: At half health the Warden wakes a little more: a Cave Echo rises beside it.

speaker: Hollow Warden
before: ...You hit like someone I knew. Small. Stubborn.
after: What is that I sense in you? NO! You are not HIM!

speaker: (battle UI)
before: A 1/1 Cave Echo rises beside the Warden.
after: A Cave Echo rises beside the Warden.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: ...Yes. The old walls do not lie. The spring at the end ran once. You would not remember.
after: Let the Paths guide you.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: Go. The house is yours to leave. Someone is waiting at the far end with a kettle on.
after: The light drains from the Warden's eyes.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I was told someone would come past the dry spring and that grumpy Warden. Nobody mentioned I'd need to wring them out.
after: And look at the state of you! I said I'd help whoever she sends along, not take in a stray.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: This isn't trust, dearie. You could be anyone's spy, and whoever pushed you into that tunnel is reckless. I don't like reckless.
after: I don't love being wrapped up in this. I told her not to go through with whatever she has planned.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: But a body in that state needs a bed, and I have far too much pie. Welcome to {town}. Questions later.
after: But a body in that state needs a bed, and I have far too much pie. I can't just leave you out on your own, now can I?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: ...I don't remember who I am. Not sure I'm worth the bed.
after: ...I don't remember who I am, or where I am. I don't even know who rescued me.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Hm. Then we start with tea and pie and work up from there.
after: Hm. Well if you don't know then I'm not telling. There must be a reason she didn't give you her name. As for here, this is {town}. We solve everything here with cards. It looks like you already have a deck.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: First, get yourself known. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back and knock.
after: If you really don't remember anything you might be here awhile. You should get aquainted with the townsfolk. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back.

speaker: (narration)
before: Beside you kneels someone hooded, very still, as if they have waited a long time.
after: Beside you kneels someone hooded. They nudge you gently, then not so gently. You look up but cannot make out their face.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.
after: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Eat. Rest. Mind the questions you ask out loud, dearie. This town has ears.
after: I don't know who you are, but I can't turn away someone in need. And you are definitely in need.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And stop staring at my stick. Four little carvings in a ring, older than you, and none of your business.
after: You can have as much pie as you like, but don't go stealing my recipe.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You are warmer than you were. Don't mistake me, dearie, I am still watching you. The watching is free.
after: I sense something within you that wasn't there before. I trust the Paths to guide you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: My pie recipe is pinned by the door, in my own hand. Round letters, careful loops. Copy it if you like. Smudge it and I will know.
after: Have you found answers to any of your questions? I can't deny, I am intrigued despite my better judgment .

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So. You're the one they sent through the old tunnel. Kettle's been on since noon.
after: Hmph... about time you showed up. {villain}'s soldiers have been out and about today.
hand_edit: designer line with {villain} for the literal Primm
